newsitem.title: UK: Care needed in interpreting Maastricht-Lamfalussy.
newsitem.headline: Care needed in interpreting Maastricht-Lamfalussy.

text.p: Care should be taken in interpreting the words of the Maastricht treaty and deviations from the reference values should be granted sparingly, Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institute said.

Speaking at a conference in London, he said that while the Maastricht treaty established two reference values which should not be exceeded -- the three percent deficit ceiling and the 60 percent debt ceiling -- it accepts deviations from these reference values on certain conditions.
"...deviations from the reference values should be granted sparingly by interpreting the words used by the treaty in a carefully restrictive way," he said.
"...compliance with the reference values should be regarded as sufficient for eligibility only if the deficit and debt ratios observed for 1997 are genuinely sustainable."
Lamfalussy said European Union should stick to both the spirit and the letter of the Maastricht treaty.
"In short, in case of doubt when applying the second and third prescriptions of the treaty, we should lean towards caution," he told the conference.
"I believe that EMU will lead to major benefits for participants, although potential costs should not be disregarded."

He said to minimise these costs and to ensure large and lasting net benefits, countries entering Monetary Union should be in a state of sustainable macroeconomic convergence and ready to improve the working of their labour markets as well as to reduce the often very substantial indirect labour costs.
